title: serving-runtime-weekly-update-kernel-kv-batching-2026-11-26
body:
Summary:
This week the serving-runtime team focused on three parallel streams: kernel optimizations for fused ops and int8 paths, KV cache improvements (eviction and warming), and dynamic batching heuristics. Primary objective was to recover and exceed prior throughput while keeping p95 latency within SLO for TL;DR workloads and to get a canary build ready for Dedicated clusters.

Highlights:
- Kernel: landed fused attention + gelu matmul kernel (PR #2345) with a 12-18% perf win for sequence lengths <= 1024 on A100. Also iterated on auto-tile selection logic to avoid pathological tilings for odd-dim models.
- KV cache: switched to a LFU-weighted eviction with a time-decay factor (configurable). Observed cache hit rate increase from ~62% -> ~79% on internal chat workload traces (better prefix reuse).
- Batching: updated adaptive batching policy to be latency-aware (soft cap at 60ms p50), and added early-flush heuristic for strict-latency routes. Reduced token-cost by 6% in mixed-traffic benchmark.

Metrics (canary bench vs baseline):
- Model: curated-open-13B, mixed prompt lengths (avg 256)
- Throughput (tokens/sec per GPU): +14%
- p50 latency: unchanged (~28ms/token)
- p95 latency: improved 9% for short requests, slight regression (~3%) for worst-case long seq > 4096 due to kernel tiling fallback
- KV cache hit rate: 62% -> 79% (chat traces)
- Unit cost estimate: ~5% reduction after batching + cache wins

Work completed this week:
- Kernel optimizations:
  - Merged fused attention + FFN matmul path (PR #2345). Primary author: Marco. Bench tests: microbench + canary harness.
  - Auto-tiling fallback added for shapes that trigger memory fragmentation (Linnea).
  - Added int8 path sanity checks to prevent silent quantization mis-rounding on fp32->int8 kernels.

- KV cache improvements:
  - Implemented LFU-weighted eviction with time decay (config flag: kv.eviction_policy=lfu_decay).
  - Cache warming job to pre-populate popular prefixes during canary rollout. Warm-up uses historical prompt buckets.
  - Instrumented cache metrics: per-model hit-rate, per-route cache footprint, eviction age histogram.

- Batching changes:
  - Adaptive batching now consults route SLO and queue depth (config: batching.adaptive=true).
  - Early-flush heuristic for routes with strict latency SLOs (client tags: latency_slo=low/med/high).
  - Stress-tested batching on mixed-traffic sim with synthetic spikes.

Blockers & Risks:
- Regression on long-sequence (>4096) p95 due to auto-tile fallback path; root cause appears to be a kernel memory layout edge-case. Current mitigation: revert to previous tiling for sequences >4096 until patch lands. (Jira INF-1123)
- Intermittent GPU OOM observed in canary when combined with aggressive cache warming on nodes with limited free memory. Mitigation: cap warming concurrently to 30% of free GPU memory; added warning logs.
- One flaky e2e test in CI related to batching timing (flaky under high host load). Tracking with flaky-test label and WIP fix from Jordan.

Decisions made:
- Canary rollout target: 5 Dedicated nodes in us-west-2 with canary traffic 5% of production. Rollout scheduled for Mon 2026-11-30 pending two fixes (tiling fallback patch + cache warming cap).
- Disable aggressive warming by default in Dedicated; opt-in via config until OOM risk fully understood.
- Keep LFU-decay as default for hosted chat routes with high prefix reuse; expose knob for customers on Dedicated.

Next week / Action items:
- Fix auto-tiling regression and run long-sequence p95 benchmark matrix (owner: Linnea, due: 2026-11-29).
- Patch cache-warming memory cap and add preflight check to skip warming on constrained nodes (owner: Jordan, due: 2026-11-28).
- Canary rollout and close monitoring with SRE oncall; dashboard alerts for cache hit-rate drop and p95 regressions (owner: Aisha, due: 2026-11-30).
- Finalize rollout playbook (rollback criteria, observability checklist, customer notification template) and share with support and sales.

Meeting notes (Weekly sync 2026-11-26):
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Linnea, Jordan, Sofia, Rafael (SRE)
- Marco demoed fused-kernel benchmark and tradeoffs; agreed to proceed to canary after tiling fix.
- Linnea reviewed KV metrics; suggested hit-rate alert when dropping >5% from baseline.
- Jordan outlined batching changes and requested extended CI window for timing-sensitive tests.
- SRE asked for preflight memory checks and canary circuit-breaker on OOM.

Standup snippets (Mon-Fri):
- Mon 2026-11-23 — Marco: landed fused kernel bench, iterating perf counters. Linnea: started auto-tile fallback implementation. Jordan: drafted batching e2e scenarios.
- Tue 2026-11-24 — Linnea: repro'd tiling regression on seq 8192; added instrumentation. Jordan: added warming cap prototype. Aisha: prepared canary ring plan.
- Wed 2026-11-25 — Marco: debugged int8 path; found small rounding diff, added guard. Linnea: working on patch for fallback. Jordan: running synthetic spike sims for batching.
- Thu 2026-11-26 — Team sync + demo. SRE ran memory safety runs. Decision: target canary after fixes.
- Fri 2026-11-27 — (planned) finalize patches, run full canary smoke.

Notes / TODOs for docs:
- Update ops-runbook with new canary checklist entries (kv warming cap, eviction policy flag).
- Add kernel perf summary to serving-runtime/perf-dashboard page.
- Link PRs and Jira to the release note draft for next Dedicated release.

If you need details on any of the PRs or want the raw bench traces, ping me (Aisha) or look at the linked artifacts.
